affectedCopies: JobEvent, JobRun, JobStep, JobWait, JobConcurrencySlot, JobCronState: engine state of the owned durable-job engine, written and read only by apps/web/lib/jobs/postgres (store.ts) behind the @/lib/jobs facade
Populated only when DPF_JOBS_ENGINE=postgres routes functions to the engine; with the flag unset (the default) nothing writes them

The same event payloads and step outputs are what Inngest stores today in its own `inngest` database (events, history, traces); routing a function here moves that copy, it does not add a new kind of data

privacyAssessment.sensitivity: internal: job event payloads and step outputs carry whatever their senders put there, mostly record identifiers (buildId, organizationId, operationId, workItemId); some may name a user id
privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: No column is a person's record. Payloads are pruned with their finished run after the retention window (7 days by default), so they are not a durable copy. Deleting a person does not need to reach these rows: they expire.
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: Not shown on any surface. Visible to database administrators only, as Inngest's own tables are today.

migration.name: 20261001210000_durable_job_engine
migration.backfill: None. One enum and six new tables nothing existing references; every function stays on Inngest until the flag routes it. IF NOT EXISTS and duplicate_object guards make a re-run harmless, so it applies cleanly against any existing data state (verified: fresh database, twice; a copy of the live schema, twice).
migration.rollback: Forward-only. With the flag unset the tables stay empty and unused; older code ignores them.
